title: Measure of cognition-certainty — evidence; moral evidence still evidence
source_text: XIV. Prioris certitudinis mensura est ipsa rei evidentia & clara perceptio, quae quo major est, eo quoque in mente certitudo major. Nam certum & evidens hoc respectu convertuntur. Ac profecto nihil etiam moraliter certum dici potest, quod non ratione aliqua sit evidens. Nam quamvis assensus certus a Philosophis dividi soleat in assensum evidentem, qualis est scientiae, & intelligentiae: & in assensum obscurum atque inevidentem, qualis est qui nascitur ex signis & indiciis, & ad quem humana impellit authoritas: tamen hic ipse est quodammodo evidens, scilicet evidentia quae moralis dicitur. Nam cum certo judicamus aliquid ita esse, ad hoc moti hominum fama, consensu & testimonio, ut in exemplis ante propositis, istud eo facimus quod intellectus noster ex variis indiciis & argumentis colligit & videt, tum fide dignos esse testes qui proferuntur, tum revera hoc & illud testimonium ab ipsis perhiberi.
pass_a_gloss: The measure of the former certainty is the very evidence and clear perception of the thing, which the greater it is, the greater also is certainty in the mind. For certain and evident in this respect are convertible. And indeed nothing even morally certain can be said which is not in some way evident. For although certain assent is wont to be divided by Philosophers into evident assent, such as that of science and intelligence, and into obscure and inevident assent, such as that which is born from signs and indications and to which human authority drives: yet this itself is in a manner evident — namely by that evidence which is called moral. For when we certainly judge that something so is, moved to this by men’s fame, consensus, and testimony, as in the examples proposed before, we do that because our intellect from various indications and arguments gathers and sees both that the witnesses brought forward are worthy of faith, and that this and that testimony is truly borne by them.
pass_b_english: Cognition-certainty measured by evidence / clear perception.
Certain ↔ evident here; even moral certainty needs some evidence.
Sign/authority assent is obscure vs scientia — yet morally evident (trustworthy witnesses).

lemmas.gloss: certain and evident in this respect are convertible
